idiom_name: reference-type entity with an immutable Id; EF Core key and change tracker for persistence identity
implementation_notes: In C# an entity is a class with an Id property, and identity is the runtime's reference equality: object.Equals on a class without an override is ReferenceEquals, so the in-memory half of the pattern is already the language default and nothing has to be built. The persistence half comes from EF Core, which maps the Id (or <Type>Id) property as the primary key, tracks at most one instance per key value (identity resolution) and explicitly recommends not overriding Equals/GetHashCode, because navigation collections that use overridden equality silently merge or duplicate instances. Keep the Id immutable from the domain's point of view (get-only or init-only), let the change tracker own loading and change detection, and override equality by id only when detached copies must compare equal - in which case give collection navigations a ReferenceEqualityComparer.
pitfalls: Overriding Equals/GetHashCode by id while EF Core compares entities by reference and tracks one instance per key duplicates entries in HashSet navigations; if you override, force ReferenceEqualityComparer for those collections.

A store-generated key is assigned at SaveChanges, so an id-based GetHashCode changes while the object sits in a dictionary or set; prefer a client-generated key (Guid or a typed id) or reference equality.

A record (record Customer(...)) synthesizes value equality over all members, so two snapshots of the same customer compare unequal once a property changes; keep records for immutable value objects and DTOs.
